sources.entry: SketchyBar - A highly customizable macOS status bar replacement. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/FelixKratz/SketchyBar) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: SketchyBar is a highly customizable, scriptable status bar replacement for macOS, aimed at users who like working with shell scripts.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a status bar for macOS whose elements can all be added, removed, or changed at any time. It offers a dynamic animation system and an event-driven scripting system for updating the bar. Elements support interactive mouse input and on-demand popup menus. It can draw arbitrary graphs and can display macOS menu bar apps as aliases. The project says it is optimized to be fast and efficient. Configuration is done through a sketchybarrc file and plugin scripts located in ~/.config/sketchybar/, and commands can also be run from the command line.
use_cases: replace the macOS menu bar with a custom status bar
show system info like time or battery in a bar
script dynamic menu bar widgets with shell scripts
draw graphs in the macOS top bar
add clickable popup menus to a menu bar
show macOS menu bar app icons as aliases
how_to_run: Follow the installation guide in the project documentation
Review the default sketchybarrc file in ~/.config/sketchybar/
Review the default plugin scripts in ~/.config/sketchybar/
Try commands directly from the command line to see how they change the bar
notable: All bar elements can be changed at any point at runtime
Forked from spacebar and rewritten; inspired by the former yabai status bar
Related projects include SbarLua (Lua API) and sketchybar-app-font (symbol font)
caveats: The README does not state platform requirements beyond macOS
Setup relies on configuration files and shell scripts, so it suits users comfortable with scripting
Full documentation is on an external website rather than in the README
